samples.instruction: Pick up the red block from the table and place it inside the blue bowl.

policy_transcripts.content:
You control a simulated robot through the provided tools. Use the current camera images, the measured robot state, and the history of this trial to complete the user's task.

Respond with exactly one tool call per turn. Every movement call must include a brief note describing what you observe and why you choose that movement. Check the next observation before deciding your next action. A commanded target is not a measurement of the position reached.

You have at most 20 model calls for this trial, including tool errors and any done or give_up call. The trial also has a separate limit of 900 robot control steps. Call done when you judge the task complete, or give_up when you judge that you cannot complete it within the remaining budget.

Use only the supplied task, robot documentation, tools, and observations. Do not request outside assistance, access source code or hidden simulator state, or use information from other trials. No feedback or learned notes from previous trials are available.

Robot documentation:
Robot: one Franka Panda arm with a parallel-jaw gripper in a tabletop simulation. The table surface is at world z=0.80 m. World +z points upward. All position targets and measured end-effector positions use the same world frame.

The move_to tool accepts absolute x, y, z, yaw, and gripper targets. Position units are meters and yaw units are radians. Valid bounds are x in [-0.30, 0.35], y in [-0.30, 0.30], z in [0.80, 1.30], and yaw in [-pi, pi]. The gripper is oriented approximately downward; yaw is its controllable rotation about world +z. Pitch and roll are not exposed as action dimensions.

Gripper commands are binary: use 0 to close and 1 to open. The reported gripper value is the measured opening normalized from 0 to 1, so holding an object may produce an intermediate measurement. In the adapter, targets below 0.35 latch closed, targets above 0.65 latch open, and intermediate targets retain the previous command. Intermediate commanded openings are not supported. Dimensions omitted from move_to are filled from the measured end-effector state by the tool layer.

The tool layer interpolates targets under its shared motion limits. The robot may not reach a target before the next observation; use the measured state and images to determine what happened. No additional settling motion is inserted after a tool call.

State fields: eef_pos is the measured end-effector position; eef_quat uses (w,x,y,z); eef_yaw is in radians; gripper is measured normalized opening; eef_state is [x,y,z,yaw,gripper]. joint_pos and joint_vel describe the seven arm joints in radians and radians per second. joint_eff contains arm actuator torques in N m, including controller compensation; it is not a fingertip contact sensor.

Cameras: front and side are fixed views; wrist moves with the hand. All are 224x224 RGB images with the top row at the top of the view. The wrist view can rotate as the hand rotates. No fixed mapping from image directions to world x/y is assumed. Each request includes the current three views and retains images from at most the two most recent observations.
Goal: Pick up the red block from the table and place it inside the blue bowl.

I am stopping rather than spending the last call on a motion that cannot finish the placement.", "hindsight": "Concrete facts for a future agent on this rig. (1) Motion is heavily truncated: the tool budget for one call is shared with the gripper, and a gripper latch costs ~80 control steps, so any move_to that includes gripper=0/1 leaves only a few steps for the arm and barely moves it; never bundle a long translation with a close/open, and never rely on a commanded target being reached. (2) Pure lateral moves of 10-20 cm advanced only 2-6 steps (~1-4 cm) in my run, so most of my 20 calls were spent on localisation rather than travel; plan at most ~8 localisation calls. (3) The block was at world (x=-0.030, y=-0.075) on the table (table top z=0.80, block ~3 cm), the blue bowl was at roughly (0.0,+0.02), i.e. only ~10 cm from the block; my early axis-calibration moves drifted to x=+0.04,y=+0.07 and wasted ~10 calls. (4) Fingertip pads sit about 2.5-3 cm below the reported eef_pos, so to straddle a 3 cm block the eef z target should be ~0.855-0.865; at eef z=0.876 the pads were still above the block top and closed on air. (5) Gripper measurement is effectively binary here: 0.98 = open, 0.016 = closed on air; a real grasp should read intermediate, so re-check that number after every close instead of trusting the images. (6) Camera axes: in the side view image-horizontal is world x (bowl/−x at left, arm base at right) and it is a good metric ruler (~0.5 mm/px at this depth); in the front view image-horizontal is also x but depth (y) is hard to read; the wrist view rotates with yaw, so do not assume image right = any fixed world axis — verify with one small single-axis move before trusting it. (7) The wrist camera looking straight down shows the finger gap and the block between the pads, which is the most reliable lateral alignment cue once the hand is low."}

policy_transcripts.content: give_up: Measured gripper opening is 0.0162, i.e. fully closed on empty air, so the block is still resting on the table at (-0.030,-0.075) and is not held. The trial is at step 783 of 900 and this is call 19 of 20: a close-only move already consumed 79 steps, so the remaining ~117 steps cannot cover a lift, a translation to the bowl and a release. I am stopping rather than spending the last call on a motion that cannot finish the placement.

trial_metadata.hindsight: Concrete facts for a future agent on this rig. (1) Motion is heavily truncated: the tool budget for one call is shared with the gripper, and a gripper latch costs ~80 control steps, so any move_to that includes gripper=0/1 leaves only a few steps for the arm and barely moves it; never bundle a long translation with a close/open, and never rely on a commanded target being reached. (2) Pure lateral moves of 10-20 cm advanced only 2-6 steps (~1-4 cm) in my run, so most of my 20 calls were spent on localisation rather than travel; plan at most ~8 localisation calls. (3) The block was at world (x=-0.030, y=-0.075) on the table (table top z=0.80, block ~3 cm), the blue bowl was at roughly (0.0,+0.02), i.e. only ~10 cm from the block; my early axis-calibration moves drifted to x=+0.04,y=+0.07 and wasted ~10 calls. (4) Fingertip pads sit about 2.5-3 cm below the reported eef_pos, so to straddle a 3 cm block the eef z target should be ~0.855-0.865; at eef z=0.876 the pads were still above the block top and closed on air. (5) Gripper measurement is effectively binary here: 0.98 = open, 0.016 = closed on air; a real grasp should read intermediate, so re-check that number after every close instead of trusting the images. (6) Camera axes: in the side view image-horizontal is world x (bowl/−x at left, arm base at right) and it is a good metric ruler (~0.5 mm/px at this depth); in the front view image-horizontal is also x but depth (y) is hard to read; the wrist view rotates with yaw, so do not assume image right = any fixed world axis — verify with one small single-axis move before trusting it. (7) The wrist camera looking straight down shows the finger gap and the block between the pads, which is the most reliable lateral alignment cue once the hand is low.
